description: Polyphonic sample player built on a high quality resampler — a loaded sample with a loop, a release section and an envelope, played at a volt per octave

params.text: Sets where in the sample playing starts, 0V to 10V across the whole file
Sets where playing stops, 0V to 10V across the whole file
Sets where the loop starts, 0V to 10V across the whole file
Sets where the loop ends, 0V to 10V across the whole file
Sets where the release section starts, 0V to 10V across the whole file
Picks what happens at the loop end: playing straight on to the sample end, looping back to the loop start, or turning round and running back to the loop start
Picks what happens when the gate is released: stopping at once, playing on to the sample end, looping from the release start to the sample end, or bouncing between them
Sets how long the envelope takes to climb to its peak, 0 to 20 seconds
Sets how long the envelope takes to fall from its peak to the sustain level, 0 to 60 seconds
Sets how long the envelope takes to fall to silence once the gate is released, 0 to 60 seconds
Sets the level the envelope starts from when the gate arrives
Sets the level the attack climbs to
Sets the level the envelope holds at while the gate is held
Bends the attack of the envelope, from fast at first through a straight line to slow at first
Bends the decay of the envelope, from fast at first through a straight line to slow at first
Bends the release of the envelope, from fast at first through a straight line to slow at first
Picks how the other four points follow the sample start point: not at all, moving with it by the same amount, or two that scale that movement by how far into the file the start point is
Sets the sample gain, 1 to 10 times
Snaps every point to the nearest place the waveform crosses zero, which takes the click out of a loop

inputs.text: A gate here plays the sample; it is polyphonic, and each channel gets its own voice
Sets the playback pitch, a volt per octave
Volts here move the sample start point, added to its knob
Volts here move the sample end point, added to its knob
Volts here move the loop start point, added to its knob
Volts here move the loop end point, added to its knob
Volts here move the release start point, added to its knob
Volts here are added to the attack time
Volts here are added to the decay time
Volts here are added to the release time
Volts here are added to the starting level of the envelope
Volts here are added to the peak level of the envelope
Volts here are added to the sustain level of the envelope
Volts here bend the attack, added to its slope knob
Volts here bend the decay, added to its slope knob
Volts here bend the release, added to its slope knob

outputs.text: The sample playing, one polyphony channel per gate

notes: nothing plays until a sample is loaded: choose Load sample from the right-click menu, or drop a wav or aiff file onto the panel
the display draws the waveform with the five points marked across it; drag up and down on it to zoom and sideways to scroll, and hold shift while dragging to zoom faster
the sample is played in mono, so a stereo file is mixed down as it is loaded, and a file recorded at another rate is converted to the engine's sample rate
menu: Load sample — opens a wav or aiff file and loads it as the sample
